# Settings reference

Every choice of the project and study editor in the admin console (**Projects & Studies**) that is
not self-explanatory has a **?** button next to its name. This page lists the same texts, grouped
as in the editor, with the key each choice writes in `project.yaml` (under `defaults:`) or
`study.yaml` (under `overrides:`). How the settings work together is explained in
[Project management](project-management.md) and [Study management](study-management.md).

Admins can read the same texts as JSON from `GET /api/admin/help`.

<!-- settings-reference:start (generated by `python -m hani2.help_texts docs/guide/settings-reference.md`) -->

## Project

| Setting | Key | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| [Kind](#setting-kind) | `kind` | What the project evaluates: Assistants (HI), opponents (HAN) or nothing (research) |

### Kind {#setting-kind}

`kind`: *What the project evaluates: Assistants (HI), opponents (HAN) or nothing (research)*

| Kind | Ranks | Typical studies |
|---|---|---|
| `assistant` | the **Assistants** (Hybrid Intelligence track) | people with an Assistant against AI opponents or each other |
| `opponent` | the **opponent agents** (Human-Agent Negotiation track) | people without an Assistant against the entrant agents |
| `none` | nothing | research studies, demonstrations, the game |

The kind decides which pool a **Paired** mode needs: `[human+assistant]` in an HI project,
`[human]` with `assistants: [none]` in a HAN project.

More: [Project management](project-management.md#what-a-project-is).

## Study

| Setting | Key | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| [Study type](#setting-type) | `type` | How participants arrive: Prolific, an online link or a lab session |

### Study type {#setting-type}

`type`: *How participants arrive: Prolific, an online link or a lab session*

| Type | Participants | Link |
|---|---|---|
| `prolific` | recruited on Prolific; their Prolific id is their name | the Prolific study URL, with Prolific's placeholders |
| `online` | anyone with the link, with or without an account | the play link, or a per-participant link |
| `lab` | in person, with a session code you hand out | the lab session link |

The type changes the links the study page offers and, for Prolific, the completion code and
return URL.

More: [Study management](study-management.md#study-types).

## Defaults

| Setting | Key | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| [Mode](#setting-study-mode) | `study_mode` | Solo (one person against an AI), Paired (two people) or Mixed; unset, it is derived from the opponents |
| [Scenario set](#setting-scenario-set) | `scenario_set` | The scenario types participants negotiate, and their order |
| [Strict scenarios](#setting-strict-scenarios) | `strict_scenarios` | Serve saved scenarios only: a missing or broken pool is an error, never a generated scenario |
| [Simple scenarios](#setting-simple-scenarios) | `simple_scenarios` | Generate scenarios with round numbers and linear or symmetric preferences |
| [Forced value on disagreement](#setting-force-reserved-value) | `force_reserved_value` | The participant's value on disagreement in every negotiation, whatever the scenario says |
| [Counted negotiations](#setting-n-required) | `n_required` | K: how many negotiations of each participant count (practice not included) |
| [Practice round](#setting-practice) | `practice` | A first negotiation that does not count |
| [Participant's role](#setting-role-rule) | `role_rule` | Which side of the scenario the participant takes |
| [Preferred roles](#setting-human-roles) | `human_roles` | For the roles rule: the role names the participant should take, in order |

### Mode {#setting-study-mode}

`study_mode`: *Solo (one person against an AI), Paired (two people) or Mixed; unset, it is derived from the opponents*

| Mode | HI project (`kind: assistant`) | HAN project (`kind: opponent`) |
|---|---|---|
| **Solo** | the human has an Assistant; the opponent is an AI agent (built-in, `:pan`, or HAN entrants) | a human without an Assistant against the entrant agents |
| **Paired** | two people, each with their own Assistant (`opponents: [human+assistant]`) | two people without Assistants (`opponents: [human]`). **It tests no HAN agent**, so its results are not ranked |
| **Mixed** | a person when someone fits, otherwise an AI opponent (for example a game) | rarely useful |

The mode does not replace the opponent pool: the pool still decides who plays. The mode is your
declared intent, and it is **checked** against the pool, the Assistant and the project's kind:

| Mode | The opponents must be | When the opponents are not set |
|---|---|---|
| Solo | no `human` / `human+assistant` entry | the default pool |
| Paired (HI) | exactly `[human+assistant]` | filled in |
| Paired (HAN) | exactly `[human]`, with `assistants: [none]` | both filled in |
| Mixed | at least one person and one AI | refused: name the pool |

A file that disagrees is refused when you save it, with a message that names both keys.

**Derived.** Leave the mode unset and it is derived from the opponents: no human entry is Solo,
only human entries is Paired, both is Mixed. Existing projects keep working unchanged.

More: [Project management](project-management.md#mode-solo-paired-or-mixed).

### Scenario set {#setting-scenario-set}

`scenario_set`: *The scenario types participants negotiate, and their order*

A scenario set is a named, ordered list of scenario types (domains). The scenario method of the
Scheduling group decides which type each negotiation takes from it; the participant then gets the
next scenario of that type. Empty: the set of the layer above.

More: [Scenarios](scenarios.md).

### Strict scenarios {#setting-strict-scenarios}

`strict_scenarios`: *Serve saved scenarios only: a missing or broken pool is an error, never a generated scenario*

With **Yes**, every negotiation uses a scenario saved in the scenario pool. When a type has no
usable saved scenario, the session reports an error instead of generating one, so every participant
of the study sees exactly the scenarios you prepared. With **No**, a missing scenario is generated.

More: [Scenarios](scenarios.md#strict-scenarios).

### Simple scenarios {#setting-simple-scenarios}

`simple_scenarios`: *Generate scenarios with round numbers and linear or symmetric preferences*

With **Yes** (the default), generated scenarios use round numbers and plain shapes of preferences
(linear or symmetric), which are easier for people to read, and only saved scenarios generated the
same way are served. With **No**, any saved scenario may be served and generated ones may use any
shape.

More: [Scenarios](scenarios.md#simple-scenarios).

### Forced value on disagreement {#setting-force-reserved-value}

`force_reserved_value`: *The participant's value on disagreement in every negotiation, whatever the scenario says*

Empty (the default): every scenario keeps its own values. A number gives the **participant** that
value on disagreement in every negotiation; the opponent keeps the scenario's. When two
participants negotiate with each other, each gets their own study's value.

The number is on the scenario's utility scale: 0 to 1 for normalised scenarios, so `0` means that
any agreement is at least as good as none (and `0` is a value, not "unset"). Saved scenarios are
never changed: the value is applied when a scenario loads, and each recorded negotiation carries the
value that was played.

More: [Project management](project-management.md#forcing-the-value-on-disagreement).

### Counted negotiations {#setting-n-required}

`n_required`: *K: how many negotiations of each participant count (practice not included)*

The number of **counted** negotiations per participant, called $K$ in the assignment rules. A
practice round comes on top. With a method that gives each participant a new Assistant each
negotiation, $K$ must not exceed the number of Assistants $N$ if each Assistant is to be used at
most once per person: the Assistant row of the Scheduling group warns when $K > N$.

More: [Study management](study-management.md#assigning-assistants-opponents-and-scenarios).

### Practice round {#setting-practice}

`practice`: *A first negotiation that does not count*

With **Yes**, each participant first plays a practice negotiation (with its own time limit). It is
recorded with `practice: true` and is left out of the counted negotiations, of the scores and of
the assignment balance.

### Participant's role {#setting-role-rule}

`role_rule`: *Which side of the scenario the participant takes*

| Rule | Role |
|---|---|
| `auto` | a role named `human`, else the scenario's suggested role, else the participant's index |
| `index` | the participant's index (the admin setting `human_index`) |
| `roles` | the first of **Preferred roles** that the scenario has, else `auto` |
| `alternate` | alternates between the roles from one negotiation to the next |
| `random` | a random role |

In Paired studies the host's side is chosen this way and the joiner takes the other one.

### Preferred roles {#setting-human-roles}

`human_roles`: *For the roles rule: the role names the participant should take, in order*

Used only with the `roles` rule: the first of these names that the scenario has is the
participant's role (for example `Buyer`). Scenarios with none of them fall back to `auto`.

## Information

| Setting | Key | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| [Participant knows](#setting-information-preferences-human) | `information.preferences.human` | Which part of their own preferences the participant sees |
| [Assistant knows](#setting-information-preferences-assistant) | `information.preferences.assistant` | Which part of the participant's preferences the Assistant knows |
| [Value on disagreement](#setting-information-preferences-reserved-value) | `information.preferences.reserved_value` | Who knows what the participant gets when there is no deal |
| [Past negotiations](#setting-information-past-negotiations-count) | `information.past_negotiations.count` | How many records of earlier negotiations in the same scenario are shown (0: none) |
| [Participant's share](#setting-information-past-negotiations-human-share) | `information.past_negotiations.human_share` | The fraction of the past negotiations the participant gets; the Assistant gets the rest |
| [Past preferences](#setting-information-past-negotiations-preferences) | `information.past_negotiations.preferences` | How the past parties' preferences relate to this negotiation's |
| [Market research](#setting-information-market-research-audience) | `information.market_research.audience` | Who gets statistics about how preferences in the scenario are usually distributed |

### Participant knows {#setting-information-preferences-human}

`information.preferences.human`: *Which part of their own preferences the participant sees*

| Value | The participant sees |
|---|---|
| `full` | the weights of the issues and the value of every option |
| `weights` | only how much each issue matters |
| `values` | only the value of the options of each issue |
| `none` | nothing: they must discover their preferences (for example from the Assistant) |

More: [Information](information.md).

### Assistant knows {#setting-information-preferences-assistant}

`information.preferences.assistant`: *Which part of the participant's preferences the Assistant knows*

The same choices as **Participant knows** (`full`, `weights`, `values`, `none`), for the
Assistant. Giving the two different parts makes them depend on each other: for example the
participant knows the weights and the Assistant knows the values.

More: [Information](information.md).

### Value on disagreement {#setting-information-preferences-reserved-value}

`information.preferences.reserved_value`: *Who knows what the participant gets when there is no deal*

`both`, `human` (only the participant), `assistant` (only the Assistant) or `none`. This is the
reserved value: no deal worth less than it should be accepted.

More: [Information](information.md).

### Past negotiations {#setting-information-past-negotiations-count}

`information.past_negotiations.count`: *How many records of earlier negotiations in the same scenario are shown (0: none)*

Each record shows how an earlier negotiation in the same scenario went. They are shared between the
participant and the Assistant by **Participant's share**.

More: [Information](information.md).

### Participant's share {#setting-information-past-negotiations-human-share}

`information.past_negotiations.human_share`: *The fraction of the past negotiations the participant gets; the Assistant gets the rest*

A number between 0 and 1. With 0.5 and 4 past negotiations, each side sees 2 different records.

More: [Information](information.md).

### Past preferences {#setting-information-past-negotiations-preferences}

`information.past_negotiations.preferences`: *How the past parties' preferences relate to this negotiation's*

| Value | The past negotiations were played with |
|---|---|
| `same` | the same preferences as this one |
| `similar` | preferences close to these (the default) |
| `different` | unrelated preferences |

More: [Information](information.md).

### Market research {#setting-information-market-research-audience}

`information.market_research.audience`: *Who gets statistics about how preferences in the scenario are usually distributed*

`none`, `assistant`, `human` or `both`.

More: [Information](information.md).

## Opponents

| Setting | Key | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| [HAN agents](#setting-opponents-han) | `opponents` | Add the entrant agents of a HAN league by year and set; the year is always written out |
| [Opponent pool](#setting-opponents-pool) | `opponents` | Who participants face at this layer; the study's mode decides which human entries are offered |

### HAN agents {#setting-opponents-han}

`opponents`: *Add the entrant agents of a HAN league by year and set; the year is always written out*

Writes an entry `:han<year>-<set>` into the opponent pool:

| Set | Agents |
|---|---|
| `all` | every entrant of that year |
| `qualified` | the qualified entrants |
| `finalists` | the finalists |
| `winners` | the winners |

**The year is always stored.** "This year" and "last year" are only labels, computed from the
project's **Year** (not from the clock): in a project of year 2027, "last year" writes
`:han2026-…`.

**Where the agents come from.** The current year (`han.current_year` in `env.json`) comes from that
year's submitted zips; every other year from the installed `han-agents` package. A year that
neither covers is greyed out ("no agents for 2025"), and a file naming one is refused when saved.

An HI study may name several years (`:han2026-finalists`, `:han2027-finalists`): every game records
the year, the source and the version of the agent it played.

More: [Project management](project-management.md#han-agents-by-year).

### Opponent pool {#setting-opponents-pool}

`opponents`: *Who participants face at this layer; the study's mode decides which human entries are offered*

The pool lists AI agents, groups (`:pan`, `:han2027-finalists`, …) and other people:

| Entry | Means |
|---|---|
| `human` | another participant without an Assistant |
| `human+assistant` | another participant with their own Assistant |

The declared **Mode** (`study_mode`) limits the human entries:

| Mode | HI project (`kind: assistant`) | HAN project (`kind: opponent`) | Research (`kind: none`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Solo | no human entry | no human entry | no human entry |
| Paired | `human+assistant` only | `human` only | `human`, `human+assistant` |
| Mixed, or not declared | both | both | both |

A Paired pool lists people only, so its AI agents are not offered either (the AI fallback has its own
pool, **Fallback opponents**). An entry already in the pool that the mode does not allow stays shown,
in red, so that it can be removed; the server refuses to save the contradiction. Without a declared
mode, the mode is derived from the pool, so every entry is offered.

More: [Project management](project-management.md#pools-of-opponents-and-assistants).

## Assignment

| Setting | Key | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| [Opponent assignment](#setting-scheduling-opponents) | `scheduling.opponents` | How each participant's opponents are chosen from the pool |
| [Assistant assignment](#setting-scheduling-assistants) | `scheduling.assistants` | How each participant's Assistants are chosen: one for all negotiations, or a new one each time |
| [Repeats](#setting-scheduling-assistant-repeats) | `scheduling.assistant_repeats` | May a person get the same Assistant twice? Off, K > N is refused for the at-most-once methods |
| [Crossing](#setting-scheduling-cross) | `scheduling.cross` | shift: cross the Assistant with the opponent so every pair meets equally often; none: no crossing |
| [Scenario assignment](#setting-scheduling-scenarios) | `scheduling.scenarios` | How each negotiation's scenario type is chosen from the scenario set |
| [K of N](#setting-assignment-k-of-n) | `n_required` | K counted negotiations per person over N Assistants: with K > N an Assistant repeats |

### Opponent assignment {#setting-scheduling-opponents}

`scheduling.opponents`: *How each participant's opponents are chosen from the pool*

The method that assigns an opponent from the pool to each negotiation of each participant. Empty
keeps the value of the layer above (the project's, then the server default). The methods are listed
below; the Scheduling methods reference has their formulas and examples.

| Method | Summary |
|---|---|
| `latin_square` | Every participant meets the pool in an order from a balanced (Williams) Latin square. |
| `random` | Each negotiation draws an opponent uniformly from the pool. |
| `cyclic` | Participant i starts with opponent i and goes round the pool in order. |
| `fixed_order` | Everyone meets the pool in the same order, the order of the pool. |
| `external` | Only an outside system decides: the participant's schedule.json names each opponent. |

More: [Scheduling](scheduling.md#opponents).

### Assistant assignment {#setting-scheduling-assistants}

`scheduling.assistants`: *How each participant's Assistants are chosen: one for all negotiations, or a new one each time*

| You want | Method | Each person gets |
|---|---|---|
| One Assistant per person (between-subjects designs, the game) | `balanced` (default), `random_fixed`, `round_robin` | one Assistant for all $K$ negotiations |
| Every Assistant once (a final evaluation: $K = N$) | `latin_square` (or `cyclic`) | every Assistant once, in a counterbalanced order |
| $K$ of $N$ Assistants (screening: $K < N$) | `balanced_subset` (or `random_subset`) | $K$ different Assistants, with totals, positions and pairs balanced |

$K$ is **Counted negotiations** and $N$ the Assistants in the pool. The methods that promise each
Assistant at most once refuse $K > N$ unless **Repeats** is on. `random_each` draws each
negotiation independently.

In a Paired study the method gives each person a **set** of Assistants, and the order is only a
preference. The methods are listed below.

| Method | Summary |
|---|---|
| `balanced` | Each human keeps one Assistant; a new human gets the one with the fewest humans so far. |
| `random_fixed` | Each human keeps one Assistant drawn at random when they first arrive. |
| `random_each` | Every negotiation draws a new Assistant at random (within-subjects). |
| `latin_square` | Every human works with every Assistant, in an order from a balanced (Williams) Latin square (within-subjects). |
| `cyclic` | Human i starts with Assistant i and goes round the pool, one Assistant per negotiation (within-subjects). |
| `balanced_subset` | Each human gets K different Assistants of the N, chosen on arrival to balance totals, pairs and positions. |
| `random_subset` | Each human gets the first K of a random order of the N Assistants. |
| `round_robin` | Human i keeps Assistant i modulo the pool size. |
| `external` | Only an outside system decides: the participant's schedule.json names the Assistant. |

More: [Scheduling](scheduling.md#assistants).

### Repeats {#setting-scheduling-assistant-repeats}

`scheduling.assistant_repeats`: *May a person get the same Assistant twice? Off, K > N is refused for the at-most-once methods*

`latin_square`, `cyclic`, `balanced_subset`, `random_subset` and `external` promise that a person
gets **each Assistant at most once**, which is possible only when $K \le N$ (counted negotiations at
most the Assistants of the pool).

| Repeats | Effect |
|---|---|
| unset or **No** | a file with $K > N$ is refused on save ("n_required = 6 negotiations but only 5 Assistants"), and so is a project change that would give one of its studies $K > N$; `random_each` is allowed unless **No** is set explicitly |
| **Yes** | the Assistants wrap around on purpose, so a person meets some of them twice |

A study already running with $K > N$ only gets a warning, and the Assistants wrap around.

When an Assistant leaves the pool during a study, each person keeps the Assistants they already
played and gets only Assistants they have not used for the rest. If too few are left, **Yes** wraps
around; otherwise the person finishes early (a `finished_early` event).

More: [Scheduling](scheduling.md#assistant-repeats).

### Crossing {#setting-scheduling-cross}

`scheduling.cross`: *shift: cross the Assistant with the opponent so every pair meets equally often; none: no crossing*

When the Assistants change every negotiation and the opponents use `latin_square` or `cyclic`, the
two rules would line up: with 5 Assistants and 5 opponents, Assistant $j$ would always meet
opponent $j$, and an Assistant's effect could not be told apart from its opponent's. With
**shift** (the default) participant $i$'s opponent sequence is shifted by a block offset

$$
d(i) = \left\lfloor i / R \right\rfloor \bmod n_o
$$

($R$: the rows of the opponents' square, $n_o$: the opponents), so over $R \cdot n_o$ participants
every (Assistant, opponent) pair occurs equally often: 50 participants for 5 × 5.

- It applies only to that combination of methods; otherwise it changes nothing.
- Each person keeps the rule they started with, so changing it in a running study changes nothing
  for people already in it.
- **none** turns it off; HANI2 then warns when the Assistant and the opponent are confounded.

More: [Scheduling](scheduling.md#crossing).

### Scenario assignment {#setting-scheduling-scenarios}

`scheduling.scenarios`: *How each negotiation's scenario type is chosen from the scenario set*

The method that picks the scenario type (the domain) of each negotiation from the scenario set.
`by_participant` gives each person one type for all their negotiations. In a Paired study the
joiner takes the host's scenario. The methods are listed below.

| Method | Summary |
|---|---|
| `by_participant` | Each participant keeps one scenario type: type = participant index mod number of types. |
| `set_order` | Negotiations follow the order of the scenario set, with a counter per participant. |
| `random` | Each negotiation draws a scenario type uniformly from the set. |
| `latin_square` | Types are counter-balanced across negotiation slots with a balanced Latin square. |
| `external` | Only an outside system decides: the participant's schedule.json names each type. |

More: [Scheduling](scheduling.md#scenarios).

### K of N {#setting-assignment-k-of-n}

`n_required`: *K counted negotiations per person over N Assistants: with K > N an Assistant repeats*

$K$ is **Counted negotiations** (`n_required`) and $N$ the number of Assistants in the pool after
the groups are expanded. The pool is the one a session would use: `assistants` of the study, else
of the project, else the one Assistant of `assistant_settings.json` ($N = 1$). `hani2 --assistants`
on a server only gives a warning in `hani2 study show`.

- With a method that keeps one Assistant per person, $K$ and $N$ are independent.
- With a method that promises each Assistant at most once per person (`latin_square`, `cyclic`,
  `balanced_subset`, `random_subset`), $K \le N$ is required: with $K > N$ the row turns orange,
  and saving is refused unless **Repeats** is on (then the Assistants wrap around and a person
  meets some of them twice).
- $K = N$ is "every Assistant once"; $K < N$ is a $K$-of-$N$ design, best with `balanced_subset`.
- `random_each` draws each negotiation independently, so repeats can happen for any $K$.

More: [Study management](study-management.md#assigning-assistants-opponents-and-scenarios).

## Pairing

| Setting | Key | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| [Where people meet](#setting-pairing-scope) | `pairing.scope` | study: only people of this study meet; project: people of every study of the project; code: only through a ?match= link |
| [How a match is formed](#setting-pairing-assign) | `pairing.assign` | cells: balance who meets whom; order: follow each person's planned order; random: anyone who fits |
| [Slack](#setting-pairing-slack) | `pairing.slack` | Cells within this count of the emptiest are treated as tied (0: strictest balance) |
| [Scenario in a cell](#setting-pairing-cell-scenario) | `pairing.cell_scenario` | type: balance scenario types (domains); name: balance single scenarios too |
| [Same-Assistant matches](#setting-pairing-allow-same-assistant) | `pairing.allow_same_assistant` | May both sides of a match use the same Assistant? |
| [When nobody fits](#setting-pairing-fallback) | `pairing.fallback` | ai: play an AI opponent; wait: keep waiting; end: skip the slot |
| [Fallback opponents](#setting-pairing-fallback-opponents) | `pairing.fallback_opponents` | The AI pool of the fallback (default: the study's AI opponents, else :pan) |

### Where people meet {#setting-pairing-scope}

`pairing.scope`: *study: only people of this study meet; project: people of every study of the project; code: only through a ?match= link*

| Scope | Who can be paired |
|---|---|
| `study` | people of the same study (the default of a declared Paired study) |
| `project` | people of every study of the project (the default otherwise; the game uses it) |
| `code` | only people who share a `?match=<code>` link; without a code nobody is met and the fallback applies |

A `?match=<code>` link pairs those who share it in every scope, unless `human_opponent_codes` is
switched off.

More: [Project management](project-management.md#pairing-defaults).

### How a match is formed {#setting-pairing-assign}

`pairing.assign`: *cells: balance who meets whom; order: follow each person's planned order; random: anyone who fits*

| Value | Rule | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `cells` | a match goes to the least-filled **cell** (scenario, Assistant at side 0, Assistant at side 1) among the people waiting | evaluation studies, the HI game (the default of a declared Paired study) |
| `order` | each person follows their planned order of Assistants strictly; two people fit only when their next planned Assistants form an allowed pair | small scripted lab sessions (it thins the pool a lot) |
| `random` | any waiting person who fits | the game; the default of a Mixed study |

Only completed matches fill a cell; an abandoned match or an AI fallback fills none.

**By mode.** A declared **Paired** study defaults to `cells` and pairs within the study. A **Mixed**
study (the game) defaults to `random` and the project-wide lobby; `cells` or `order` set here makes
its matches balanced too. A **Solo** study has no pairing, and the editor hides this block.

The study's Assistant method gives each person a **set** of Assistants rather than a slot:
one-per-person methods give that one Assistant for every match, the at-most-once methods the first
K of the person's sequence minus the used ones, `random_each` the whole pool, `external` the
Assistants of the person's `schedule.json` slots.

More: [Project management](project-management.md#pairing-defaults).

### Slack {#setting-pairing-slack}

`pairing.slack`: *Cells within this count of the emptiest are treated as tied (0: strictest balance)*

With `cells`, a joiner could always be sent to the emptiest cell, but then who meets whom becomes
predictable. Every candidate whose cell count is within `slack` of the minimum counts as tied, and
the tie is broken by the other balance terms and finally at random.

- `0`: the strictest balance, the most predictable pairing;
- `1` (default): nearly as balanced, and nobody can aim at a particular person.

More: [Project management](project-management.md#pairing-defaults).

### Scenario in a cell {#setting-pairing-cell-scenario}

`pairing.cell_scenario`: *type: balance scenario types (domains); name: balance single scenarios too*

A match cell is (scenario, Assistant at side 0, Assistant at side 1). With `type` (the default) the
scenario is the domain, and the single scenario (which preferences were used) is recorded but not
balanced. With `name`, single scenarios are balanced too, which multiplies the number of cells by
the scenarios per type: with 5 Assistants, 3 domains and 5 scenarios each, 60 cells become 300.

More: [Project management](project-management.md#pairing-defaults).

### Same-Assistant matches {#setting-pairing-allow-same-assistant}

`pairing.allow_same_assistant`: *May both sides of a match use the same Assistant?*

**No** (the default) in evaluation studies: a match of an Assistant against itself says nothing
about it compared with the others. **Yes** in the game, where an invited guest plays with the
inviter's Assistant, so the two necessarily share one.

More: [Project management](project-management.md#pairing-defaults).

### When nobody fits {#setting-pairing-fallback}

`pairing.fallback`: *ai: play an AI opponent; wait: keep waiting; end: skip the slot*

What happens when nobody fits within `human_opponent_wait` seconds:

| Value | The person |
|---|---|
| `ai` (default) | plays their committed Assistant against an AI opponent from the fallback pool. The Assistant then counts as used for them; the game fills no cell and is ranked with the Solo games |
| `wait` | keeps waiting (the same as `human_opponent_fallback: false`; for supervised lab sessions) |
| `end` | skips the slot: they move on to their next Assistant, or finish early with the completion code |

When `human_opponent_fallback` is also set in an `env.json` and disagrees, the file is refused. To
keep a supervised session waiting today, set `human_opponent_fallback: false` in the study's
`env.json`.

More: [Project management](project-management.md#pairing-defaults).

### Fallback opponents {#setting-pairing-fallback-opponents}

`pairing.fallback_opponents`: *The AI pool of the fallback (default: the study's AI opponents, else :pan)*

AI entries only (agents and groups such as `:pan`); human entries are refused.

More: [Project management](project-management.md#pairing-defaults).

## Scores

| Setting | Key | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| [Scores](#setting-scores) | `scores` | The scores of this project or study: the built-ins (read-only) and your own |
| [Criteria](#setting-scores-criteria) | `scores.criteria` | Every number a score can use: metric columns, questionnaire answers and other scores |
| [Preview](#setting-scores-preview) | `scores.preview` | The score on the current games, before saving: weights in effect, dropped parts, its distribution, the top entrants |
| [Track](#setting-scores-track) | `scores.track` | hi ranks Assistants, han ranks opponent agents, any fits both |
| [Weights](#setting-scores-weights) | `scores.weights` | Each component's share in %, which must sum to 100 %; Normalise rescales them |
| [Direction](#setting-scores-direction) | `scores.direction` | higher or lower is better; required when the criterion has none |
| [Normaliser](#setting-scores-normaliser) | `scores.normaliser` | How a value is mapped to [0, 1] before it is weighted; preset from the criterion |
| [Missing values](#setting-scores-missing) | `scores.missing` | renormalise: rescale the parts present; zero: a missing value is 0; skip_game: the game does not count |
| [Minimum coverage](#setting-scores-min-coverage) | `scores.min_coverage` | A part present in fewer than this share of some entrant's games is dropped for everyone |
| [Zero if](#setting-scores-zero-if) | `scores.<key>.zero_if` | Criteria that, when 1, make the score 0 for the game (for example opponent_failed) |
| [Needs an Assistant](#setting-scores-needs-assistant) | `scores.<key>.needs_assistant` | true: the score is empty for sessions without an Assistant |
| [Scores enabled](#setting-scores-enabled) | `scores_enabled` | Which scores this project's (or study's) boards, results and exports compute and show |
| [Same-Assistant games](#setting-scores-same-assistant) | `scores.<key>.same_assistant` | How boards count a game where both people used the same Assistant: once, or not at all |

### Scores {#setting-scores}

`scores`: *The scores of this project or study: the built-ins (read-only) and your own*

A **score** is a weighted mean of criteria, each first mapped to $[0, 1]$ with 1 as the best value,
so every score is in $[0, 1]$.

- **Built-in** scores are read-only. **Duplicate** copies one into this file, where you can change
  it.
- A study can add scores and redefine the project's by key.
- A score with a problem (an unknown criterion, a missing direction, a cycle) is left out and named
  in the warnings.

More: [Project management](project-management.md#defining-a-score).

### Criteria {#setting-scores-criteria}

`scores.criteria`: *Every number a score can use: metric columns, questionnaire answers and other scores*

Criteria are grouped by source:

| Source | Cost | What |
|---|---|---|
| `hard` | live | measured when the game ends (outcomes, behaviour) |
| `soft` | judge | rated by the offline language-model judge |
| `subjective` | questionnaire | the bundled questionnaire's scales |
| `questionnaire` | questionnaire | items (`q_<id>`) and scales (`scale_<name>`) of the forms this project uses |
| `score` | — | other scores (a score may contain a score) |

Each shows its **direction**, its default **normaliser**, its **cost** and, when asked, its
**coverage** (the share of the current games that have a value). A post-session answer is credited
to the Assistant only when each participant used one Assistant throughout; otherwise it is greyed
out for HI scores, with the reason.

More: [Criteria](criteria.md).

### Preview {#setting-scores-preview}

`scores.preview`: *The score on the current games, before saving: weights in effect, dropped parts, its distribution, the top entrants*

The preview computes the score being built on the games the board of this project (or study) reads,
as the board would rank them, and updates a moment after each change. Nothing is saved.

| Part | Shows |
|---|---|
| Weights in effect | each component's share after the coverage rule, summing to 100 % |
| Dropped | components present in fewer than **Minimum coverage** of some entrant's games, left out for everyone |
| Distribution | how the score's values over the counted games fall into ten bins of [0, 1], with the mean and median |
| Top entrants | the first five by the score's mean, with the 95 % interval and the games counted |

Weights that do not yet sum to 100 % are previewed rescaled. A score with the track `hi` or `han`
is previewed on that track's games. The preview needs games: a new project shows "no games yet".
Admins only (`POST /api/admin/scores/preview`).

More: [Project management](project-management.md#previewing-a-score).

### Track {#setting-scores-track}

`scores.track`: *hi ranks Assistants, han ranks opponent agents, any fits both*

| Track | The score ranks |
|---|---|
| `hi` | the Assistants |
| `han` | the opponent agents |
| `any` | either (the default) |

An HI score may not use post-session answers of participants who used several Assistants.

More: [Project management](project-management.md#defining-a-score).

### Weights {#setting-scores-weights}

`scores.weights`: *Each component's share in %, which must sum to 100 %; Normalise rescales them*

Weights are $\ge 0$ and must sum to **100 %** (1, to within $10^{-6}$). Save works only then;
**Normalise** rescales the weights so that they sum to 100 % while keeping their proportions. A
weight of 0 keeps a component in the definition without using it.

The score of a game is

$$
S = \sum_i w_i \, n_i(x_i)
$$

where $n_i$ is the component's normaliser, oriented by its direction.

More: [Project management](project-management.md#defining-a-score).

### Direction {#setting-scores-direction}

`scores.direction`: *higher or lower is better; required when the criterion has none*

Most criteria know whether higher values are better. Descriptive ones (`n_offers`,
`negotiation_seconds`, the shares of move types, …) do not, and a score that uses one must say
which way is better. With `lower`, every normaliser is turned around ($1 - \cdot$).

More: [Project management](project-management.md#defining-a-score).

### Normaliser {#setting-scores-normaliser}

`scores.normaliser`: *How a value is mapped to [0, 1] before it is weighted; preset from the criterion*

| Normaliser | Rule | Default for |
|---|---|---|
| `bounded` | $\frac{x - lo}{hi - lo}\ \text{clipped to } [0, 1]$ | Columns with known bounds: `[0, 1]`, `0 or 1`, `1–7`, `[−1, 1]`, utilities, every questionnaire item and scale with its own bounds. |
| `advantage` | $\min(1, \max(0, x))$ | The `*_advantage` columns: no better than no deal (or worse) is 0, the best outcome is 1. |
| `reciprocal` | $\frac{s}{s + x}$ | Unbounded values where lower is better (counts, seconds, tokens, distances, US dollars). |
| `saturating` | $\frac{x}{x + s}$ | Unbounded values where higher is better, and unbounded values without a direction. |
| `percentile` | $\frac{\#\{r < x\} + \tfrac12 \#\{r = x\}}{n}$ | Any criterion, on request: the share of the reference games with a lower value (ties count half). |
| `clip` | $\frac{x - lo}{hi - lo}\ \text{clipped to } [0, 1]$ | Any criterion, on request, with your own bounds. |

With direction `lower`, every rule is turned around ($1 - \cdot$). The scale $s$ of `reciprocal`
and `saturating` is the median of the project's **frozen reference** (`hani2 scores freeze`), so the
median game scores 0.5 and adding games never changes past scores.

More: [Project management](project-management.md#mapping-every-value-to-0-1).

### Missing values {#setting-scores-missing}

`scores.missing`: *renormalise: rescale the parts present; zero: a missing value is 0; skip_game: the game does not count*

| Value | A missing value | Example: `human_advantage` 0.6 (weight 50 %), `ja_overall` missing (50 %) |
|---|---|---|
| `renormalise` (default) | is left out; the weights present are rescaled to sum to 1 | 0.6 |
| `zero` | counts as 0 | 0.3 |
| `skip_game` | the game gets no value for this score | none |

Whatever the policy, `<score>_coverage` is the share of the weight whose values were present.

More: [Project management](project-management.md#missing-values).

### Minimum coverage {#setting-scores-min-coverage}

`scores.min_coverage`: *A part present in fewer than this share of some entrant's games is dropped for everyone*

A component that is present in fewer than `min_coverage` (default 0.5) of **some** entrant's games
is dropped for **every** entrant, and the remaining weights are rescaled to sum to 1, so everyone is
scored on the same parts. For example, if one Assistant's participants skipped the questionnaire,
its items are left out for all Assistants rather than counting only for some.

More: [Project management](project-management.md#coverage-across-entrants).

### Zero if {#setting-scores-zero-if}

`scores.<key>.zero_if`: *Criteria that, when 1, make the score 0 for the game (for example opponent_failed)*

A list of criteria; when one of them is **1** in a game, the score of that game is **0** (with
coverage 1), whatever its components say. The built-in `han_outcome` has
`zero_if: [opponent_failed]`: an opponent agent that ended the session by failing gets 0.

```yaml
zero_if: [opponent_failed]
```

Default: none. Every entry must be a known criterion.

More: [Project management](project-management.md#rules-for-failures-and-sessions-without-an-assistant).

### Needs an Assistant {#setting-scores-needs-assistant}

`scores.<key>.needs_assistant`: *true: the score is empty for sessions without an Assistant*

With `needs_assistant: true`, a game whose human played without an Assistant has **no value** for
this score (and no coverage), so it neither helps nor hurts anyone. The built-in `hi_assistant`,
`hi_team` and `hi_interaction` have it. Default: `false`.

More: [Project management](project-management.md#rules-for-failures-and-sessions-without-an-assistant).

### Scores enabled {#setting-scores-enabled}

`scores_enabled`: *Which scores this project's (or study's) boards, results and exports compute and show*

Unset, every built-in score and every score defined in the project and the study is enabled. The
project sets the default and a study can override it. An enabled score is computed together with the
scores inside it.

More: [Project management](project-management.md#which-scores-a-study-uses).

### Same-Assistant games {#setting-scores-same-assistant}

`scores.<key>.same_assistant`: *How boards count a game where both people used the same Assistant: once, or not at all*

In a game where both sides used the **same Assistant** (for example a participant against the guest
they invited, who plays with their Assistant), the two utilities split one deal between copies of one
Assistant, so the game says little about it compared with the others.

| Value | Boards |
|---|---|
| `once` (default) | the game counts **once**, as the mean of its two rows |
| `skip` | the game is left out of this score |

The built-in `utility` has `skip` (and a copy of it keeps that).

More: [Project management](project-management.md#which-games-count).

## Leaderboard

| Setting | Key | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| [Leaderboard](#setting-leaderboard) | `leaderboard` | The board of this project (all its chosen studies) or of this study |
| [Track](#setting-leaderboard-track) | `leaderboard.track` | Who is ranked: Assistants (hi) or opponent agents (han) |
| [Source](#setting-leaderboard-source) | `leaderboard.source` | game: the games people played (default); tournament: the simulated table |
| [Studies](#setting-leaderboard-studies) | `leaderboard.studies` | Which studies of this project feed the project board (default: all) |
| [Rows from other projects](#setting-leaderboard-include) | `leaderboard.include` | Studies of other projects whose games of one stratum join this board |
| [Sort options](#setting-leaderboard-sort-options) | `leaderboard.sort_options` | What end users may rank by: enabled scores or criteria with a direction |
| [Default sort](#setting-leaderboard-default-sort) | `leaderboard.default_sort` | The key a board is ranked by when the viewer does not choose; one of the sort options |
| [Columns](#setting-leaderboard-columns) | `leaderboard.columns` | The values each entry shows: scores, criteria, and counts (games, participants, …) |
| [Switches for end users](#setting-leaderboard-user-options) | `leaderboard.user_options` | The switches end users get, each with its allowed values |
| [Switch defaults](#setting-leaderboard-defaults) | `leaderboard.defaults` | The value of each switch when the viewer does not choose |
| [Visibility](#setting-leaderboard-visibility) | `leaderboard.visibility` | Who may see the board: public, participants (signed-in users) or admins |
| [Minimum games](#setting-leaderboard-rules-min-games) | `leaderboard.rules.min_games` | Counted games an entrant needs before it is ranked (below: "not ranked yet") |
| [Minimum players](#setting-leaderboard-rules-min-participants) | `leaderboard.rules.min_participants` | Distinct players, not counting the Assistant's own team, an entrant needs to be ranked |
| [Cap per pair](#setting-leaderboard-rules-max-games-per-pair) | `leaderboard.rules.max_games_per_pair` | At most this many games of one entrant between the same two people (empty: no cap) |
| [Cap per player](#setting-leaderboard-rules-max-games-per-participant) | `leaderboard.rules.max_games_per_participant` | At most this many games of one entrant by the same person (empty: no cap) |
| [Leave out own-team games](#setting-leaderboard-rules-exclude-own) | `leaderboard.rules.exclude_own` | Leave out games where a team plays its own Assistant (default: count them) |
| [Adjustment](#setting-leaderboard-rules-adjust) | `leaderboard.rules.adjust` | relative: cell-adjusted means (default); balanced: the mean of the cell means |
| [Confidence level](#setting-leaderboard-rules-ci) | `leaderboard.rules.ci` | The level of the bootstrap confidence intervals (default 0.95) |

### Leaderboard {#setting-leaderboard}

`leaderboard`: *The board of this project (all its chosen studies) or of this study*

A **project board** pools the studies it names (and rows taken in from other projects); a **study
board** shows one study. The project sets the `leaderboard` block, and a study overrides it key by
key for its own board. One set of rules serves every view: the pages, the admin console and the
leaderboard API that a trusted website reads.

More: [Project management](project-management.md#leaderboards).

### Track {#setting-leaderboard-track}

`leaderboard.track`: *Who is ranked: Assistants (hi) or opponent agents (han)*

| Value | Entrants | Strata |
|---|---|---|
| `hi` | the Assistants (their entrant id from the group file, else their spec) | `combined`, `solo`, `paired` |
| `han` | the opponent agents | `alone` (no Assistant), `vs_team` (people with an Assistant), `both` (pooled) |

Unset: `han` for a project of kind `opponent`, else `hi`.

More: [Project management](project-management.md#configuring-a-board).

### Source {#setting-leaderboard-source}

`leaderboard.source`: *game: the games people played (default); tournament: the simulated table*

- `game` (default): every counted game of the board's studies, ranked with the rules below.
- `tournament`: the table of simulated participants (the goal rate of each Assistant, per persona),
  ranked by goal rate only; it has no switches, and a request for another sort or a switch gets a 400.

More: [Project management](project-management.md#configuring-a-board).

### Studies {#setting-leaderboard-studies}

`leaderboard.studies`: *Which studies of this project feed the project board (default: all)*

A list of study names, for example `[play, prolific-03]`. Add new studies as they start. A study board
always shows its own study only.

More: [Project management](project-management.md#configuring-a-board).

### Rows from other projects {#setting-leaderboard-include}

`leaderboard.include`: *Studies of other projects whose games of one stratum join this board*

Each entry names a study of another project and the stratum its games join, for example
`{study: HI2027/play, stratum: vs_team}` on a HAN board: the HI games played against this year's HAN
agents count for those agents in the `vs_team` stratum, apart from the official `alone` stratum.

More: [Project management](project-management.md#rows-from-other-projects).

### Sort options {#setting-leaderboard-sort-options}

`leaderboard.sort_options`: *What end users may rank by: enabled scores or criteria with a direction*

End users may sort only by these keys; admins may sort by any enabled score or criterion. Each key
must be enabled (`scores_enabled`) in every study the board reads; a criterion needs a direction
(higher or lower is better). A score is ranked by its entrant-level mean (cell-adjusted or
cell-balanced, see *Adjustment*); a criterion by its mean in its own direction.

More: [Project management](project-management.md#configuring-a-board).

### Default sort {#setting-leaderboard-default-sort}

`leaderboard.default_sort`: *The key a board is ranked by when the viewer does not choose; one of the sort options*

Must be one of `sort_options`. Unset: the first sort option.

More: [Project management](project-management.md#configuring-a-board).

### Columns {#setting-leaderboard-columns}

`leaderboard.columns`: *The values each entry shows: scores, criteria, and counts (games, participants, …)*

Scores and criteria (each with its mean and confidence interval), and the counts `games`,
`participants`, `guests`, `abandon_rate` and `cost_usd`. Unset: the sort options, then games and
participants.

More: [Project management](project-management.md#configuring-a-board).

### Switches for end users {#setting-leaderboard-user-options}

`leaderboard.user_options`: *The switches end users get, each with its allowed values*

| Switch | Values |
|---|---|
| `games` | `all`, `people` (games against a person), `ai` (games against an AI opponent) |
| `stratum` | HI: `combined`, `solo`, `paired`; HAN: `alone`, `vs_team`, `both` |
| `window` | `all`, `last_<n>_days` (for example `last_30_days`) |

A switch that is not listed is not shown, and its default applies. A request for a value that is
not allowed is refused (HTTP 400), so a website can only show the views the project allows.

More: [Project management](project-management.md#configuring-a-board).

### Switch defaults {#setting-leaderboard-defaults}

`leaderboard.defaults`: *The value of each switch when the viewer does not choose*

Unset: `games: all`, the track's first stratum (`combined` or `alone`) and `window: all`. A default must be one of the switch's allowed values.

More: [Project management](project-management.md#configuring-a-board).

### Visibility {#setting-leaderboard-visibility}

`leaderboard.visibility`: *Who may see the board: public, participants (signed-in users) or admins*

| Value | Who |
|---|---|
| `public` | anyone, no sign-in or token needed |
| `participants` (default) | signed-in users, and a website with an API token |
| `admins` | admins, and a website with an API token |

No board ever shows a user name or a participant index.

More: [Project management](project-management.md#visibility).

### Minimum games {#setting-leaderboard-rules-min-games}

`leaderboard.rules.min_games`: *Counted games an entrant needs before it is ranked (below: "not ranked yet")*

Counted over every counted game of the board, whatever the switches show, so an entrant does not move in and out of the ranking when a viewer changes a switch. Default 10.

More: [Project management](project-management.md#which-games-count).

### Minimum players {#setting-leaderboard-rules-min-participants}

`leaderboard.rules.min_participants`: *Distinct players, not counting the Assistant's own team, an entrant needs to be ranked*

Players marked as the Assistant's own team (`own` in their group file) do not count towards this minimum. Default 3.

More: [Project management](project-management.md#which-games-count).

### Cap per pair {#setting-leaderboard-rules-max-games-per-pair}

`leaderboard.rules.max_games_per_pair`: *At most this many games of one entrant between the same two people (empty: no cap)*

Games over the cap are left out, the latest first, and counted under `excluded: cap`.

More: [Project management](project-management.md#which-games-count).

### Cap per player {#setting-leaderboard-rules-max-games-per-participant}

`leaderboard.rules.max_games_per_participant`: *At most this many games of one entrant by the same person (empty: no cap)*

Games over the cap are left out, the latest first, and counted under `excluded: cap`.

More: [Project management](project-management.md#which-games-count).

### Leave out own-team games {#setting-leaderboard-rules-exclude-own}

`leaderboard.rules.exclude_own`: *Leave out games where a team plays its own Assistant (default: count them)*

Own-team games count by default; the *Minimum players* rule keeps a team from ranking its Assistant alone. With this on, they are left out and counted under `excluded: own team`.

More: [Project management](project-management.md#which-games-count).

### Adjustment {#setting-leaderboard-rules-adjust}

`leaderboard.rules.adjust`: *relative: cell-adjusted means (default); balanced: the mean of the cell means*

A cell is a scenario with an opponent (Solo), or a scenario, a side and an opposing Assistant
(Paired).

- `relative` (default): each game's value minus its cell's mean over all entrants, plus the overall
  mean, so the numbers stay on the values' scale. Best when entrants played different, uneven cells
  (a game).
- `balanced`: the mean of the entrant's cell means. Best for planned studies where every entrant
  plays every cell.

More: [Project management](project-management.md#confidence-intervals-and-ties).

### Confidence level {#setting-leaderboard-rules-ci}

`leaderboard.rules.ci`: *The level of the bootstrap confidence intervals (default 0.95)*

A percentile bootstrap that resamples participants. Two entrants whose intervals overlap the leader's are shown as tied with it ("=2").

More: [Project management](project-management.md#confidence-intervals-and-ties).

<!-- settings-reference:end -->
